All protected and conserved areas

Of the 782 native vascular plants known from the region, 569 (73%) have been recorded in at least one protected or conserved area, from provincial parks and ecological reserves to old growth management areas and private conservation lands. The remaining 213 are so far known only from outside protected areas.

Key Biodiversity Areas

2 published, 2 of them globally significant · 0 proposed · 23,630 hectares

Key Biodiversity Areas mark the places that matter most for the persistence of species and ecosystems. The region holds 2 published Key Biodiversity Areas, identified chiefly for the birds that gather in Howe Sound and along the Squamish River. 399 of the region's 782 native vascular plants (51%) have been recorded within them.

399 native species · 51% of the native flora
7 species of conservation concern
10,123 native plant records

  2. Squamish River 245

This is a preliminary assessment. Sampling effort is uneven across the region and the records have gaps, but it offers a starting point for tracking how well the region’s plant diversity is protected. You can help improve it by sharing your observations with the Átl’ḵa7tsem/Howe Sound Biosphere Region iNaturalist project.

The map shows protected and conserved areas by category. Click an area on the map or in the chart to see the plants recorded there, or a category in the legend or the chart to see those recorded across all its areas. Key Biodiversity Areas are outlined in cream. Choose Unprotected native plant diversity to see where the native plants not yet found in any protected area have been recorded.

Protected areas are from the Canadian Protected and Conserved Areas Database (Environment and Climate Change Canada), and Key Biodiversity Areas from KBA Canada (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
